questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which Maurya ruler issued the famous edict at Kalinga after being deeply moved by the devastation of the Kalinga War?
questions.explanation: Ashoka fought the Kalinga War around 261 BCE. Horrified by the massive bloodshed, he issued the 13th Major Rock Edict describing his remorse and his subsequent adoption of the policy of Dhamma.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Mansabdari' system introduced during the reign of Akbar was primarily used to ?
options: organise the military and civil administration
questions.explanation: The Mansabdari system was a graded ranking system introduced by Akbar to organise both the military and civil services. Mansabdars held ranks (mansab) denoting the number of cavalry they were required to maintain.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which of the following Vedas contains the 'Gayatri Mantra' in its original form?
questions.explanation: The Gayatri Mantra (Rigveda 3.62.10) is originally found in the Rigveda. It is addressed to the solar deity Savitr and is composed by the sage Vishwamitra.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Poorna Swaraj' resolution was passed at the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in the year ?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Session of the INC held in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the Poorna Swaraj resolution. As a result, 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which Sultan of Delhi is credited with introducing the 'market reform' system to control prices of essential commodities in the 14th century?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji established a comprehensive market control system with separate markets (mandis) for different goods, fixed prices (rate lists), and appointed controllers such as Shahna-i-Mandi and the secret intelligence officer Barids to enforce them.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Non-Cooperation Movement formally adopted as a resolution?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was formally endorsed by the Indian National Congress at its Nagpur Session in December 1920, under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The Simon Commission, which arrived in India in 1928, was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily because ?
options: it was headed by a military officer
it sought to divide Bengal again
it proposed abolition of the Indian Army
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission was an all-British committee with no Indian representation, which deeply hurt Indian sentiments and led to a widespread boycott across party lines.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were executed on 23 March 1931 in connection with which case?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were tried and hanged in the Lahore Conspiracy Case, which arose from the killing of British police officer J.P. Saunders in 1928.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The slogan 'Do or Die' was given by Mahatma Gandhi in the context of which movement?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi gave the historic call 'Do or Die' on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee, marking the launch of the Quit India Movement.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Who among the following presided over the very first session of the Indian National Congress held in 1885?
questions.explanation: Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee) presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in December 1885, becoming its first president.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to the frequent floods it causes in the region?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because it frequently changes its course and causes devastating floods in the plains of Bihar every year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of soil is most suitable for the cultivation of cotton and is predominantly found in the Deccan Plateau region of India?
questions.explanation: Black soil, also known as Regur soil or cotton soil, is formed from basaltic lava and has high moisture-retention capacity, making it ideal for cotton cultivation. It is predominantly found in the Deccan Plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The retreating monsoon season in India is associated with which of the following phenomena?
questions.explanation: During the retreating monsoon (October?December), the South-West monsoon withdraws and winds blow from the North-East direction. These North-East monsoon winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and bring rainfall to the Coromandel Coast, particularly Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Shillong Plateau is an outlier of the peninsular plateau that lies separated from the main plateau by the valley of which river?
questions.explanation: The Shillong Plateau is considered a detached part of the Peninsular Plateau. It is separated from the main Peninsular Plateau by the alluvial plains of the Brahmaputra river (Assam plains), which lie between the two landmasses.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Sundari trees, from which the Sundarbans get their name, belong to which type of natural vegetation found in India?
questions.explanation: Sundari trees (Heritiera fomes) are a characteristic species of tidal or mangrove forests. The Sundarbans delta in West Bengal is the world's largest mangrove forest and derives its name from these Sundari trees.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which Five Year Plan in India was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model and gave priority to rapid industrialisation?
questions.explanation: The Second Five Year Plan (1956?61), formulated by P.C. Mahalanobis, was based on the Harrod-Domar model and emphasised rapid industrialisation with focus on heavy industries.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) refers to the minimum percentage of a commercial bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that must be maintained in the form of which of the following?
questions.explanation: SLR is the proportion of NDTL that banks must keep in liquid assets such as gold, cash, or RBI-approved securities, as mandated under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following Indian states was the first to benefit most significantly from the Green Revolution, particularly in wheat production?
questions.explanation: Punjab was the leading beneficiary of the Green Revolution in India, achieving dramatic increases in wheat output due to high-yielding variety seeds, irrigation, and modern agricultural inputs from the late 1960s.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: If Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at market prices is Rs. 5,00,000 crore and Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) is Rs. 10,000 crore, what will be the Gross National Product (GNP) at market prices?
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + NFIA. Here, GNP = 5,00,000 + 10,000 = Rs. 5,10,000 crore. NFIA is added to GDP to arrive at GNP.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which type of unemployment is most commonly found in the agricultural sector of India, where workers appear to be employed but their marginal productivity is zero or near zero?
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are engaged in a job than actually required, making the marginal productivity of extra workers zero. It is a widespread feature of India's agricultural sector.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Constitutional Remedies provided, which Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 grants citizens the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. Ambedkar famously described Article 32 as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are contained in which Part?
questions.explanation: Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36?51). They are non-justiciable but fundamental to governance.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment Act were the Fundamental Duties of citizens added to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added Part IVA (Article 51A) to the Constitution, incorporating ten Fundamental Duties of citizens on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as provided in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 80 of the Constitution provides that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of not more than 250 members ? up to 238 elected representatives of States and Union Territories, and up to 12 members nominated by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (effective from April 24, 1993) inserted Part IX and the 11th Schedule into the Constitution, granting constitutional recognition to Panchayati Raj institutions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gland in the human body is known as the 'master gland' because it regulates the functioning of most other endocrine glands?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland, located at the base of the brain, is called the 'master gland' because it secretes hormones that regulate the activity of other endocrine glands such as the thyroid, adrenal, and gonads.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following substances is used to test whether a given solution is acidic or basic in nature?
questions.explanation: Litmus is a natural indicator derived from lichens. It turns red in acidic solutions and blue in basic solutions, making it a standard tool for testing the acidic or basic nature of a substance.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A person suffering from myopia (short-sightedness) is unable to see distant objects clearly. Which type of lens is used to correct this defect?
questions.explanation: In myopia, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is used to correct this defect as it diverges the incoming light rays so that they focus correctly on the retina.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin leads to the disease 'Scurvy', characterized by bleeding gums and weakness?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Vitamin C is essential for the synthesis of collagen, and its lack leads to symptoms like bleeding gums, bruising, and poor wound healing.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: According to Newton's third law of motion, when a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils backward. This phenomenon is an example of which principle?
questions.explanation: The recoil of a gun is a classic example of the law of conservation of momentum. Before firing, the total momentum of the gun-bullet system is zero. After firing, the forward momentum of the bullet is equal and opposite to the backward momentum of the gun, keeping the total momentum zero.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article 25% above its cost price and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. Marked Price = 100 ? 1.25 = 125. After 20% discount, SP = 125 ? 0.80 = 100. Profit = SP - CP = 100 - 100 = 0. Hence, there is no profit and no loss.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times of itself?
questions.explanation: If a sum doubles in 8 years, the interest earned equals the principal in 8 years, giving a rate of 100/8 = 12.5% per year. To become 4 times, interest needed = 3 ? Principal, so Time = 3 ? 8 = 24 years.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: The ratio of the ages of Ravi and Suresh is 4 : 5. After 6 years, the ratio of their ages will be 6 : 7. What is the present age of Ravi?
questions.explanation: Let Ravi = 4x and Suresh = 5x. After 6 years: (4x+6)/(5x+6) = 6/7. Cross-multiplying: 7(4x+6) = 6(5x+6) ? 28x+42 = 30x+36 ? 2x = 6 ? x = 3. Ravi's present age = 4?3 = 12 years.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A trader bought 80 oranges for Rs. 240 and sold them at the rate of 5 oranges for Rs. 18. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: CP of 80 oranges = Rs. 240. SP of 5 oranges = Rs. 18, so SP of 80 oranges = (18/5) ? 80 = Rs. 288. Profit = 288 ? 240 = Rs. 48. Profit% = (48/240) ? 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete the same work in 18 days. If they work together, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: A's one day work = 1/12, B's one day work = 1/18. Combined one day work = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36. Total days = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct Sandhi Vichchhed of the word '???'?
questions.explanation: ???' is formed by Ayadi Sandhi: ?? + ?? = ???, where '?' before a vowel changes to '??'.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct meaning of the idiom '?????? ?? ????'?
questions.explanation: ?????? ?? ????' means a person who outwardly appears friendly but secretly betrays ? a trusted traitor or backstabber.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct antonym of the word '????'?
questions.explanation: ????' means easy or accessible; its correct antonym is '??????', meaning difficult to reach or inaccessible.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence from the options below.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence is '???? ???? ????? ?? ??? ???' Here '?????' is a feminine noun and the verb '?? ??? ??' agrees with it correctly.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: In the word '????????', which type of Samas (compound) is used?
questions.explanation: ????????' means 'according to one's ability' (????? ?? ??????). The first word '???' is an indeclinable (avyaya), making this an Avyayibhav Samas.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'OBSCURE'.
questions.explanation: Obscure' means not clearly expressed or difficult to understand, which is closest in meaning to 'Vague'. The other options ? Vivid, Candid, and Radiant ? carry opposite or unrelated meanings.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'FRUGAL'.
questions.explanation: Frugal' means careful about spending money or using resources sparingly. Its antonym is 'Lavish', which means spending freely and extravagantly. 'Thrifty' and 'Prudent' are synonyms of Frugal, not antonyms.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the correct option to fill in the blank: She was tired, ______ she continued working until midnight.
questions.explanation: The sentence expresses a contrast ? being tired and still continuing to work. The coordinating conjunction 'yet' is used to show contrast between two ideas, making it the correct choice here. 'So' implies result, 'for' implies reason, and 'nor' is used for negative addition.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the one word that best substitutes the given phrase: 'A person who is unable to pay their debts'.
questions.explanation: Bankrupt' specifically refers to a person who is legally declared unable to pay their debts. A 'Miser' hoards money, a 'Creditor' is one who lends money, and a 'Philanthropist' is one who donates generously to charity.
questions.hindi_question: ??? ?? ???????? ?? ??? ???? ??????? ?? ???? ?????: 'A person who is unable to pay their debts'.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error: (A) The committee have / (B) reached a decision / (C) after a long / (D) deliberation. (No error ? E)
questions.explanation: Committee' is a collective noun that, in standard formal/Indian English usage in competitive exams, takes a singular verb. The correct form is 'The committee has', not 'The committee have'. All other parts of the sentence are grammatically correct.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 4, 9, 20, 43, 90, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern is: each term is multiplied by 2 and then 1 is added alternately subtracted: 4?2+1=9, 9?2+2=20, 20?2+3=43, 43?2+4=90, 90?2+3=183. More precisely: 4?9 (?2+1), 9?20 (?2+2), 20?43 (?2+3), 43?90 (?2+4), 90?183 (?2+3). The differences are 5, 11, 23, 47, 93 ? each difference is approximately doubled plus 1: 5?2+1=11, 11?2+1=23, 23?2+1=47, 47?2-1=93, so next term = 90+93=183.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code language, MARKET is written as NBSLFU. Using the same logic, how will BRIDGE be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted one position forward in the alphabet: M+1=N, A+1=B, R+1=S, K+1=L, E+1=F, T+1=U ? NBSLFU. Applying the same rule to BRIDGE: B+1=C, R+1=S, I+1=J, D+1=E, G+1=H, E+1=F ? CSJEHF.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Suresh says, 'The person in this photo is the only son of the father of my sister's brother.' How is the person in the photograph related to Suresh?
questions.explanation: Suresh's sister's brother is Suresh himself. The father of Suresh is his own father. The only son of Suresh's father is Suresh. So the person in the photograph is Suresh himself.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Ramesh starts from point A, walks 8 km towards the North, then turns right and walks 6 km, then turns right again and walks 8 km. How far is he from point A and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Ramesh walks 8 km North, then 6 km East (right turn), then 8 km South (right turn). The northward and southward distances cancel out (8 km each). He is left 6 km to the East of point A.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they appear to differ from commonly known facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s). Statements: All pens are books. Some books are copies. Conclusions: I. Some pens are copies. II. Some copies are books.
questions.explanation: From 'All pens are books' and 'Some books are copies', we cannot conclude that some pens are copies (the books that are copies may not be pens) ? so Conclusion I does not follow. However, 'Some books are copies' directly implies 'Some copies are books' by conversion ? so Conclusion II follows.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), free LPG connections are provided to women belonging to which category?
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016 to provide free LPG connections to women from Below Poverty Line (BPL) households, reducing their dependence on traditional cooking fuels.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) of India operates under the administrative control of which ministry?
questions.explanation: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) was established in 2009 under the NIA Act and functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is India's central counter-terrorism law enforcement agency.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The Khelo India Youth Games is organized by the Government of India primarily to achieve which objective?
options: Revive sports culture at grassroots level
Select players for Olympic squad directly
questions.explanation: Khelo India Youth Games was launched under the Khelo India programme to revive sports culture at the grassroots level across India and identify and nurture sporting talent from a young age.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in India is regulated and managed by which organization?
questions.explanation: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is managed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India's 'Mission LiFE' initiative, launched by PM Narendra Modi, primarily focuses on which aspect?
questions.explanation: Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) was launched by PM Modi at COP26 in 2021. It promotes an individual-driven global movement that encourages mindful and deliberate utilization of resources to protect the environment.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed near which region of the Moon in August 2023?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to achieve a soft landing in that region of the Moon.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme launched in 2023 is primarily aimed at providing support to which group?
questions.explanation: PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched on 17 September 2023 to provide end-to-end support including skill training, toolkits, credit access, and market linkage to traditional artisans and craftspeople such as carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, and weavers.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in which year?
questions.explanation: India (along with Pakistan) was admitted as a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at the Astana Summit held in June 2017, elevating its status from observer to full member.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'One Nation One Ration Card' scheme in India allows beneficiaries to access their food entitlement from any Fair Price Shop across the country. This scheme is implemented under which act?
questions.explanation: The One Nation One Ration Card scheme is implemented under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013. It allows migrant workers and their families to access subsidised food grains from any PDS outlet in the country using biometric authentication.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Padma Vibhushan' is the second highest civilian award of India. Which of the following correctly describes the order of India's three Padma awards from highest to lowest?
options: Padma Shri > Padma Bhushan > Padma Vibhushan
Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri
Padma Bhushan > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Shri
Padma Shri > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan
questions.explanation: The three Padma awards in descending order are: Padma Vibhushan (second highest civilian honour after Bharat Ratna), followed by Padma Bhushan, and then Padma Shri as the third highest.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor issued the farman in 1717 granting the English East India Company the right to trade duty-free in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar issued a farman in 1717 granting the English East India Company duty-free trading rights in Bengal, which was a major milestone in British commercial expansion in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President of India declare a National Emergency on the ground of armed rebellion?
questions.explanation: Article 352 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to proclaim a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion (the term 'armed rebellion' replaced 'internal disturbance' by the 44th Amendment).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Loktak Lake, which is the largest freshwater lake in northeastern India and is known for its floating 'phumdis', is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Loktak Lake is situated in Manipur and is famous for its phumdis ? floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter. The Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park, is located on this lake.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In India, the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is maintained by commercial banks as a percentage of their:
questions.explanation: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is the minimum percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) that every commercial bank in India must maintain in the form of liquid assets such as gold, government securities, or cash.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesized in the human body when the skin is exposed to sunlight, and its deficiency causes rickets in children?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin upon exposure to ultraviolet B (UVB) rays from sunlight. Its deficiency leads to improper calcium absorption, causing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Kashi Vishwanath Corridor' project, inaugurated in December 2021, connects the Kashi Vishwanath temple to which river ghat in Varanasi?
questions.explanation: The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in December 2021, directly connects the Kashi Vishwanath temple to Dashashwamedh Ghat on the banks of the Ganga river in Varanasi.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The classical dance form 'Mohiniyattam', which is known for its graceful, swaying movements, belongs to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and originates from Kerala. It is a feminine dance form characterized by gentle, swaying body movements and white-and-gold costumes.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Durand Cup, one of the oldest football tournaments in the world, was first organised in India in which year?
questions.explanation: The Durand Cup was first held in 1891 in Shimla, organized by Sir Mortimer Durand, then Foreign Secretary of India. It is the third oldest football tournament in the world, after the FA Cup and the Scottish Cup.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress in 1929 was the demand for 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) formally adopted as the goal of the Congress?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress, held in December 1929 under the presidentship of Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the Purna Swaraj resolution. The tricolour flag was unfurled on 31 December 1929 and 26 January was declared Independence Day.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which among the following is classified as a 'biosphere reserve' by UNESCO and is located in the state of Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is located in Uttarakhand and has been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Biosphere Reserve. It includes the Nanda Devi National Park and the Valley of Flowers National Park.
